Some news that has made me smile this morning. 😊
I've just received my Microsoft MVP renewal for a third year, and I honestly feel incredibly honoured and humbled.
The Microsoft data community has changed my life.

Ten years ago, I was a Padawan trying to make sense of Power Query and Power BI through free blog posts, YouTube videos and community events. I couldn't afford expensive courses, so the community became my Jedi Academy. 

Today, finding myself on the other side as an MVP, speaker and business owner, I'm reminded just how life-changing that generosity can be.
Fast forward to today, and I run my own data consultancy doing work I genuinely love. 

It's given me opportunities I never imagined possible – travelling the world, speaking at conferences, running marathons, building a business around something I'm passionate about, and even having my dog by my side for most of the working day. That's a pretty special feeling.

One of the highlights of every fortnight is recording the #Unpivot podcast, chatting about #PowerBI, #Fabric, #Excel and all the random conversations that inevitably follow. 😄 Today we're recording with someone who played a huge part in my own journey—one of the people who made me realise I'd found my tribe: a community of people who genuinely enjoy sharing knowledge and helping others succeed. I can't wait to share that episode.

This evening feels particularly meaningful because I'm presenting for the Vancouver Power BI & Modern Excel Meetup, hosted by Ken Puls.
It's difficult to overstate the impact Ken has had on my career. I devoured his courses while I was learning Power Query and Excel.
To now be speaking for his user group (again) feels like one of those full-circle moments.

My session is:
You've Built the Model. Now What? Turning Semantic Models into Insights, Automation and AI
We'll explore how semantic models can become much more than reporting datasets by extending them with automation, AI, governance, notebooks and analytics to unlock even more business value.

A huge thank you to everyone who shares their knowledge so freely. You never know whose career you're helping to shape.
Hopefully, in some small way, I'm now able to give a little of that back.
May the MVPForce be with you. ✨

A huge thank you to the awesomeness that is Rie Merritt together with all team and all my fellow #MVPs, it's so cool being part of your tribe 🥰

It's a question we hear a lot on #Unpivot, and it's one I've asked myself when feeling overwhelmed.  With so many new tools appearing every week, it's easy to think you need to learn everything before you begin.
You don't.
When people ask me where to start, this is usually what I suggest:
🎙️ Find a couple of podcasts, books or courses that explain AI in a way that makes sense to you. Listen regularly and you'll soon start recognising the patterns and possibilities.
👥 Go to meetups, whether online or in person. They're a brilliant way to see what other people are building and to ask questions in a friendly environment.
🤝 Find a community. Some of the biggest steps in my own career have come from learning alongside other people who were curious enough to give something new a go.
💡 Most importantly, find one real-life problem that matters to you. It could be something at work that takes too long, or something at home that you enjoy doing. When AI helps solve a problem you genuinely care about, learning becomes much easier.
🌱 Start small. Don't try to build the perfect solution on day one. Save yourself ten minutes. Automate one task. Write one prompt. Learn one new thing. Those small wins build confidence surprisingly quickly.
That's how I'd recommend anyone starts with AI.
What's the first real problem AI helped you solve?
